correctness.rationale: The claim uses the unscaled edge-incidence realization of C_n in the zero-sum Euclidean hyperplane and fixed t>0. Every proper selected-edge set is a forest, with path-block Gram determinant equal to its vertex count; wedge volume is the square root of the product. Rooting a cyclic composition at a deleted edge gives the exact factor n/(n-k) and all V_k including V_0=1 and V_(n-1)=n sqrt(n). The identity W_n=-n t^n[z^n]log(1-F(z)/t), F(z)=sum sqrt(j) z^j, has a unique strictly dominant simple root rho in (0,1) by aperiodicity. Uniform complex-parameter singularity extraction gives the logarithmic moment generating function n[u-log rho(te^u)+log rho(t)]+O(c^n), so E K=n(1-1/mu)+O(c^n), Var K=n sigma^2/mu^3+O(c^n), and the CLT. An independent Gram/forest-composition comparison for every k at n=3..8 reproduced the coefficients. The analytic argument, not finite checks, proves the arbitrary-n limits.
residual_risks: The proof uses a fixed t>0 and cannot establish varying-parameter uniformity; numerical constants depend on edge scaling.
No independent formal proof of the analytic quasi-power estimate was performed; mathematical reconstruction verifies its conditions.
